chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
the fasting person who rinses his mouth, he said: 'He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on swallowing saliva while rinsing the mouth during fasting?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the precise mechanism of breaking the fast during *madmadah* (rinsing the mouth). By requiring the fasting person to spit out the accumulated saliva three times before swallowing, the Imam ensures that no residual moisture or food particles remain in the throat, thereby preventing accidental ingestion that would invalidate the fast. This specific detail highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on meticulous adherence to the physical conditions of fasting as derived from the Imams' practical guidance.
